Otwock Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Karczew, Poland

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Otwock in the late 19th century, with the community's growth closely tied to the town's development as a health resort; by 1932, 10,019 Jews made up over 68% of the population, most murdered at Treblinka in August 1942. This cemetery, located in nearby Karczew's Anielin farm area, was likely established around 1908 and served both Otwock's community and patients from local hospitals and sanatoriums. Unusually, it remained active after the war - Fajwel Felder was buried here in 1947, Abram Miński in 1950 - and Holocaust victims were exhumed from other locations and reburied on the site. Wartime looters used tombstones for construction and grinding discs, while graves were later plundered for bones and skulls sought by medical students. Since 2002, the Committee for the Remembrance of the Jews of Otwock and Karczew has led regular cleanup, with support from a Ministry of Health rehabilitation center and American Baptist volunteers who helped mark the boundaries with granite boulders.
